historical_claims.anchor: During its formation, the parent deposits proteins, RNAs, nutrients and other components in particular places.
In the early fruit-fly embryo, many rounds of nuclear division occur before the embryo is partitioned into a conventional layer of separate cells.
An especially important experiment was published in 1924 by Hilde Mangold and Hans Spemann.
The use of differently pigmented embryos helped distinguish donor from host contributions.
The result revealed what became known as the embryonic organizer:
This is the intuitive idea of a morphogen, a molecule whose concentration can contribute to different developmental outcomes across space.
Maternal gene products, including the protein Bicoid, help establish differences along the egg's head-to-tail axis.
Then groups of regulators called gap genes, pair-rule genes and segment-polarity genes help elaborate the pattern.
The famous Antennapedia example can cause leg-like structures to form where an antenna would normally be.
During gastrulation, sheets and groups of cells rearrange to establish tissue layers and axes.
Regulatory networks can stabilize patterns of expression.
In a small nematode such as Caenorhabditis elegans, researchers were able to observe embryonic cell divisions systematically and produce detailed lineage maps,
Genetic barcodes can mark descendants of earlier cells.
With lineage recording and molecular profiles combined, researchers can ask whether different tissue types arose from shared ancestors and when their expression programs diverged.
A single-cell RNA profile does not literally reveal a cell's entire past or future.
